{{short description|Belgian physicist (born 1950)}}
'''Gustaaf Van Tendeloo''' (born 1950), or '''Staf Van Tendeloo'''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=van Tendeloo |first1=Gustaaf |last2=Amelinckx |first2=Severin |title=Structural studies on Superconducting materials and fullerites by electron microscopy |journal=Advanced Materials |date=September 1993 |volume=5 |issue=9 |pages=620–629 |doi=10.1002/adma.19930050904|bibcode=1993AdM.....5..620V }}</ref> is a Belgian physicist known for his contributions to electron microscopy, [[electron crystallography]], and the physics of materials.<ref name=bio>{{cite book |date=27 December 1996 |doi=10.1002/9783527620524.fmatter|isbn=978-3-527-29473-2 |chapter=Frontmatter |title=Handbook of Microscopy }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title='Onze microscoop toont een nanodeeltje in 3D' |url=https://www.eoswetenschap.eu/natuurwetenschappen/onze-microscoop-toont-een-nanodeeltje-3d |access-date=2024-03-31 |website=EOS Wetenschap |language=nl}}</ref> In 2011, his group reported the first atomically resolved reconstruction of a [[nanoparticle]] in 3D.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Van Aert |first1=Sandra |last2=Batenburg |first2=Kees J. |last3=Rossell |first3=Marta D. |last4=Erni |first4=Rolf |last5=Van Tendeloo |first5=Gustaaf |date=2011 |title=Three-dimensional atomic imaging of crystalline nanoparticles |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature09741 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=470 |issue=7334 |pages=374–377 |doi=10.1038/nature09741 |pmid=21289625 |bibcode=2011Natur.470..374V |issn=0028-0836}}</ref>

Van Tendeloo was born in [[Lier, Belgium]]. He obtained his [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] in physics from the [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]] (VUB; 'Free University of Brussels') in 1972, followed by his doctorate from the [[University of Antwerp]] in 1974 under the supervision of Severin Amelinckx. He received an aggregation from the VUB in 1981. Since 1972, Van Tendeloo has been associated with the University of Antwerp, where he is the professor of [[solid-state physics]]. Additionally, he serves as Professor of the Physics of Materials at the University of Antwerp. In 1986 he became part-time professor at the VUB and since 1994 he has been a full professor at the University of Antwerp. Since 2003, he has been the head of the EMAT (Electron Microscopy of Materials) laboratory on electron microscopy.<ref name=bio /><ref name=zar />

Throughout his career, Van Tendeloo has undertaken significant research endeavors both domestically and internationally, including research stints at the University of California, Berkeley, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the [[Université de Caen]].<ref name=bio /> He is a member of the [[Royal Flemish Academy of Belgium for Science and the Arts]] since 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://kvab.be/sites/default/rest/?q=leden/id/979&_=popup&width=768&height=720&iframe=true |access-date=2024-03-31 |title=Staf van Tendeloo {{!}} KVAB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Members {{!}} KVAB |url=https://kvab.be/en/members?page=14 |access-date=2024-03-31 |website=kvab.be}}</ref> He received the Dr. De Leeuw-Damry-Bourlart Prize from the [[Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO)]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-03-16 |title=Eurotapes: P. Van Tendeloo receives Dr. De Leeuw-Damry-Bourlart Award by King Philippe of Belgium – Leitat's Projects Blog |url=https://projects.leitat.org/home/eurotapes-professor-van-tendeloo-receives-excellence-award-dr-de-leeuw-damry-bourlart-2015-king-philippe-belgium/ |access-date=2024-03-31 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023, He received an honorary doctorate degree from the [[University of Zaragoza]].<ref name=zar>{{Cite web |title=Gustaaf Van Tendeloo, referente mundial en microscopía electrónica de transmisión, ha sido investido doctor honoris causa por la Universidad de Zaragoza |url=https://www.unizar.es/actualidad/vernoticia_ng.php?id=73601&idh= |access-date=2024-03-30 |website=www.unizar.es}}</ref>
